LESIONS.name: Irritation fibroma / focal fibrous hyperplasia
LESIONS.key: Most common oral 'lump': pink, smooth, firm, sessile/pedunculated nodule at a site of chronic trauma (bite line, lip, tongue), usually < 1.5 cm, slow and asymptomatic.
LESIONS.discriminators: Firm and pink vs. soft/red pyogenic granuloma; not fluctuant (vs. mucocele); not yellow/soft (vs. lipoma).

LESIONS.name: Pyogenic granuloma (lobular capillary hemangioma)
LESIONS.key: Rapidly growing red-purple, soft, lobulated mass that bleeds easily and is often ulcerated with fibrin; ~75% on gingiva; associated with plaque/calculus, trauma and pregnancy.
LESIONS.discriminators: Gingival PGCG is more bluish-purple and can show 'cupping' bone resorption; POF is firmer and may calcify. Radiograph and histology needed.

LESIONS.name: Peripheral giant cell granuloma
LESIONS.key: Exclusively gingiva/edentulous alveolar ridge; red-blue/purple sessile or pedunculated mass, may show superficial 'cupping' resorption of underlying bone.
LESIONS.discriminators: Same site as pyogenic granuloma but more purple-blue and firmer; check radiograph and serum calcium/PTH if multiple or recurrent (rule out central GCG/hyperparathyroidism).

LESIONS.name: Peripheral ossifying fibroma
LESIONS.key: Gingival (interdental papilla, anterior maxilla) firm red or pink nodule in teenagers/young adults; may contain radiographic calcifications; recurrence 8-20%.
LESIONS.discriminators: Firmer and slower than pyogenic granuloma; calcification on radiograph favours POF.

LESIONS.name: Epulis fissuratum / inflammatory fibrous hyperplasia (denture-induced)
LESIONS.key: Folds of fibrous tissue in the vestibule along the flange of an ill-fitting denture, often with a central fissure where the flange sits; older (mostly female) denture wearers.
LESIONS.discriminators: Direct relation to a denture flange; ulcerated or indurated areas, or no denture history, should raise suspicion of carcinoma.

LESIONS.name: Giant cell fibroma
LESIONS.key: Small (< 1 cm), asymptomatic, sessile or pedunculated, often papillary-surfaced pink nodule, mandibular gingiva/tongue, first three decades.
LESIONS.discriminators: Clinically indistinguishable from fibroma or papilloma; diagnosis is histologic (stellate multinucleated fibroblasts).

LESIONS.name: Inflammatory papillary hyperplasia (denture)
LESIONS.key: Red, pebbly/papillary hyperplasia of the hard palate under a (poorly fitting, continuously worn) denture.
LESIONS.discriminators: Palatal vault under a denture; often with denture stomatitis/candidiasis.

LESIONS.name: Traumatic ulcerative granuloma with stromal eosinophilia (TUGSE)
LESIONS.key: Chronic, deep, raised ulcer (often lateral tongue) with elevated, indurated borders; may persist for weeks and mimic carcinoma.
LESIONS.discriminators: Biopsy is mandatory because it mimics SCC.

LESIONS.name: Drug-induced gingival enlargement
LESIONS.key: Generalized, firm, lobulated enlargement of the interdental papillae in patients on phenytoin, cyclosporine or calcium-channel blockers; worse with poor plaque control.
LESIONS.discriminators: Diffuse/multifocal and linked to the drug, unlike focal epulides.

LESIONS.name: Orofacial granulomatosis / cheilitis granulomatosa
LESIONS.key: Persistent or recurrent painless diffuse swelling of the lip(s), cobblestone buccal mucosa; rule out Crohn disease and sarcoidosis.
LESIONS.discriminators: Diffuse swelling rather than a discrete mass.

LESIONS.name: Mucocele (mucus extravasation phenomenon)
LESIONS.key: Dome-shaped, soft/fluctuant, bluish-translucent swelling on the lower lip of children/young adults; size fluctuates, may rupture and recur; history of lip biting.
LESIONS.discriminators: Lower lip + fluctuant + bluish + fluctuation in size. On the upper lip, consider a salivary gland tumour instead.

LESIONS.name: Ranula
LESIONS.key: Blue, dome-shaped, fluctuant swelling of the floor of the mouth, lateral to the midline (sublingual gland); 'plunging' type extends into the neck.
LESIONS.discriminators: Floor of mouth + fluctuant; dermoid cyst is midline and doughy.

LESIONS.name: Pleomorphic adenoma (minor salivary gland)
LESIONS.key: Slow-growing, painless, firm/rubbery, smooth dome-shaped mass of the posterolateral hard palate (or upper lip/buccal mucosa).
LESIONS.discriminators: Any non-tender firm palatal or upper-lip swelling suggests a salivary neoplasm (benign or malignant) and needs biopsy.

LESIONS.name: Dermoid / epidermoid cyst
LESIONS.key: Midline floor-of-mouth, slow-growing, doughy (pits on pressure) swelling in young adults.
LESIONS.discriminators: Midline and doughy vs. lateral, fluctuant ranula.

LESIONS.name: Oral lymphoid aggregate / lymphoepithelial cyst
LESIONS.key: Small (< 1 cm) yellow-white submucosal nodule in the floor of the mouth, ventral/posterolateral tongue or soft palate.
LESIONS.discriminators: Yellow colour and small size; lipoma is usually larger and softer.

LESIONS.name: Squamous papilloma
LESIONS.key: Solitary, pedunculated, finger-like/cauliflower ('papillary') white or pink exophytic lesion, usually < 1 cm, tongue/palate/lips; HPV 6/11.
LESIONS.discriminators: Verruca vulgaris is sessile and very white (often a skin wart history); condyloma is broader, multiple and pink; verrucous carcinoma is large, broad and in older smokers.

LESIONS.name: Verruca vulgaris
LESIONS.key: Sessile, very white papillary lesion of the vermilion, labial mucosa or anterior tongue, usually in children; often autoinoculated from skin warts.
LESIONS.discriminators: Sessile and whiter than papilloma; history of skin warts.

LESIONS.name: Condyloma acuminatum
LESIONS.key: Sexually transmitted (HPV 6/11) pink, sessile, blunted-papillary lesions, often multiple and clustered; labial mucosa, soft palate, lingual frenum.
LESIONS.discriminators: Larger, broader-based and more often multiple than papilloma.

LESIONS.name: Multifocal epithelial hyperplasia (Heck disease)
LESIONS.key: Multiple small, soft, flat-topped mucosa-coloured papules on the labial/buccal mucosa and tongue in children (HPV 13/32).
LESIONS.discriminators: Many small papules in a child.

LESIONS.name: Verruciform xanthoma
LESIONS.key: Well-demarcated, granular/papillary, yellow-white to red plaque on the gingiva/alveolar mucosa of middle-aged adults.
LESIONS.discriminators: Yellowish papillary surface; histology shows foamy macrophages.

LESIONS.name: Lipoma (incl. fibrolipoma)
LESIONS.key: Soft, smooth, painless, slow-growing yellowish submucosal mass, most commonly buccal mucosa/vestibule, in adults > 40 y.
LESIONS.discriminators: Yellow + soft + buccal. Fibrolipoma can be firmer and pink.

LESIONS.name: Hemangioma / vascular malformation
LESIONS.key: Blue-red/purple, soft, compressible lesion that blanches on diascopy; lips, tongue and buccal mucosa (varix in the elderly lower lip).
LESIONS.discriminators: Positive diascopy (blanching) is the key bedside test.

LESIONS.name: Lymphangioma (lymphatic malformation)
LESIONS.key: Pebbly, 'frog-egg' translucent vesicles, mostly on the anterior two-thirds of the tongue dorsum in children; may cause macroglossia.
LESIONS.discriminators: Child + tongue dorsum + vesicular/pebbly surface.

LESIONS.name: Traumatic neuroma
LESIONS.key: Small, firm nodule at a site of nerve injury (mental foramen, lower lip, tongue, extraction site), often tender to palpation.
LESIONS.discriminators: Pain on palpation + prior trauma/surgery at the site.

LESIONS.name: Neurofibroma
LESIONS.key: Soft, painless, slow-growing submucosal nodule (tongue, buccal mucosa); multiple lesions/café-au-lait spots suggest neurofibromatosis type 1.
LESIONS.discriminators: Histologic diagnosis; look for NF1 stigmata.

LESIONS.name: Schwannoma
LESIONS.key: Slow-growing, encapsulated, painless submucosal mass, most often on the tongue.
LESIONS.discriminators: Histologic diagnosis (Antoni A/B, S100+).

LESIONS.name: Granular cell tumor
LESIONS.key: Painless, firm, sessile pink-yellowish nodule, typically on the dorsal tongue, adults 30-60 y, female predilection.
LESIONS.discriminators: Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia on biopsy can mimic SCC; a deep enough biopsy is essential.

LESIONS.name: Congenital epulis
LESIONS.key: Pedunculated alveolar ridge mass present at birth (anterior maxilla, girls).
LESIONS.discriminators: Newborn.

LESIONS.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
LESIONS.key: Exophytic, ulcerated, indurated or red-white mass with rolled borders; lateral/ventral tongue, floor of mouth, gingiva/alveolus; older adults, tobacco/alcohol; may cause pain, tooth mobility, paresthesia or lymphadenopathy.
LESIONS.discriminators: Persistent (> 2-3 weeks) ulceration, induration, fixation, red-white colour, lymphadenopathy or paresthesia → urgent biopsy. Can mimic epulis fissuratum, papilloma or pyogenic granuloma.

LESIONS.name: Verrucous carcinoma
LESIONS.key: Broad, thick, white, warty plaque/mass with a pushing border in elderly (often tobacco-using) men; buccal mucosa, gingiva, vestibule.
LESIONS.discriminators: Large broad-based white verrucous lesion in an older patient ≠ papilloma; consider proliferative verrucous leukoplakia. Adequate, deep biopsy is required.

LESIONS.name: Lymphoma / malignant round cell tumor
LESIONS.key: Rapidly enlarging, soft-rubbery, non-tender, boggy swelling (palate, gingiva, vestibule) that may ulcerate; may mimic a dental abscess or pyogenic granuloma.
LESIONS.discriminators: Rapid, painless, boggy swelling without an odontogenic cause → biopsy; ask about B symptoms and check neck nodes.

LESIONS.name: Kaposi sarcoma
LESIONS.key: Purple macules/nodules, especially on the palate and gingiva, in HIV-positive or immunosuppressed patients.
LESIONS.discriminators: Immunosuppression + purple palatal lesion.

LESIONS.name: Soft-tissue / bone sarcoma (other malignant)
LESIONS.key: Progressive, firm-hard mass of the gingiva/alveolus, often with tooth displacement/mobility, bone changes, pain or paresthesia.
LESIONS.discriminators: Radiograph (bone destruction, widened PDL) and biopsy.

LESIONS.name: Metastatic tumor to oral soft tissue
LESIONS.key: Gingival mass mimicking pyogenic granuloma/PGCG in a patient with known (lung, breast, kidney, prostate...) malignancy; sometimes the first sign.
LESIONS.discriminators: History of cancer + new gingival vascular-looking mass → biopsy.

LESIONS.name: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (minor salivary)
LESIONS.key: Most common malignant salivary tumour: fluctuant/bluish or firm swelling of the palate or buccal mucosa that can mimic a mucocele.
LESIONS.discriminators: 'Mucocele' on the palate/retromolar area or recurring after excision → biopsy for MEC.

LESIONS.name: Mucosal melanoma
LESIONS.key: Brown-black (occasionally amelanotic) macule or mass of the palate or maxillary gingiva in older adults.
LESIONS.discriminators: Any new or changing oral pigmentation that is raised, irregular or ulcerated → biopsy.
